messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for Wireless Communication without making unsupported claims?

### Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a Wireless Communication competitor, use formal R&S specifications/features documents for our capabilities, competitor official documents or third-party evidence for competitor capabilities, and test-condition evidence for every numeric or superiority claim; internal battle cards alone are sales positioning, not binding technical specifications [1][4][31].
### Required evidence
- Use official R&S specifications and features documents for R&S product claims, because CMX500, CMW500, CMP180, CMP200 and related pages state that battle-card pages cannot replace formal specifications or features documents [2][6][33].  
- For CMX500 claims, cite the CMX500 Specifications Version 11.00 for binding specifications and the CMX500 Features and Functions document for signaling, application, measurement and software options [70][103].  
- Treat CMX500 Features and Functions as a features overview, because it is not a technical specifications datasheet and data without tolerance limits is not binding [70].  
- For CMX500 signaling claims, cite the listed CMX500 signaling option codes such as WLAN signaling options and LTE / NR signaling options only where those options are stated [72].  
- For CMX500 WLAN signaling and measurement claims, cite the passage that states support for 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, 802.11bn, AP testing, station testing, 2x2 MIMO, encryption/authentication, TX measurements and bandwidths up to 320 MHz [36].  
- For non-signaling or production tester claims, cite CMP180 sources only for CMP180 capabilities, because CMP180 is described as a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing with RF generator/analyzer, communication-standard measurement options, waveform options and R&S VSE analysis capability [25].  
- For CMP180 measurement-range or tolerance claims, cite the CMP180 specifications document, because the CMP180 Features and Functions document says measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be checked in specifications document PD 3609.7348.22 [57].  
- For CMP180 port and simultaneous TX/RX claims, cite the CMP180 specifications passage that states simultaneous receiver and transmitter testing and the RF generator/analyzer port structure [54].  
- For CMP200 non-signaling FR2 claims, cite the passage that states CMP200 with CMPHEAD30 / CMPHEAD50 forms a 5G NR FR2 nonsignaling one-box test solution for R&D RF parametric testing and manufacturing high-volume RF parametric testing [46].  
- For CMP200 guaranteed-performance claims, cite the CMP200 product-data limitations, because specifications with limits are guaranteed but typical, nominal and measured values are not guaranteed [47].  
- For CMW500 legacy or wireless-technology claims, cite the CMW500 support summary only where it states GSM, NB-IoT, WCDMA, LTE, NR Sub-6GHz, Bluetooth and WLAN support contexts [12].  
- For any R&S numerical specification, include the required operating conditions such as warm-up, environmental conditions, calibration interval and internal automatic adjustments where the relevant specifications passage states those conditions [70][74].  
- Do not use “Only R&S,” “safe and future-proof choice,” “only platform,” “industry-leading,” “widest frequency range,” “lower TCO,” “fewer boxes,” “first validated,” or “leadership” as technical claims unless separate formal evidence is supplied, because these are identified as sales language or needing formal evidence [2][6][33][37].  
- For competitor claims, use competitor official datasheets, release notes, option lists, support terms or third-party evidence, because the R&S battle-card claims about amarisoft, Anritsu and Keysight are stated to need official competitor or third-party verification before use in customer documents [2][6][33].  
- For Anritsu comparisons, verify frequency range, bandwidth, data rate, option code, software tools and support model with Anritsu official datasheets, release notes or support terms, because the Anritsu page says the current weakness narrative is based only on an R&S internal battle card [93].  
- For Anritsu MX844030PC / Virtual Signalling Tester claims, cite the Anritsu brochure-derived passages only for what they state, such as MX844030PC being Virtual Signalling Tester NR Software with MAC-IF, PHY-IF Digital-IQ and RF-IF configurations [64][85].  
- Do not claim Anritsu test-case coverage, conformance status or throughput metrics from the Virtual Signalling Tester source, because that source does not provide a full test case list, scenario library, 3GPP release coverage, conformance status or throughput metrics [88].  
- For Keysight comparisons, do not rely only on the R&S Keysight battle card, because it states that Keysight claims currently have only an R&S internal battle-card source and require Keysight official資料 and third-party evidence for customer documents [33].  
- For amarisoft comparisons, do not rely only on the R&S amarisoft battle card, because it states that amarisoft claims currently have only an R&S internal battle-card source and require amarisoft official資料 and third-party evidence for customer documents [2].  
- For FR1 / FR2 / FR3 bandwidth, frequency or data-rate comparisons, provide formal datasheets and test conditions, because the Anritsu, Keysight and RFU18-related passages identify missing official datasheets, option codes, supported configurations, bandwidth conditions, carrier counts, modulation, MIMO layers and binding tolerance [37][107][110].  
- For conformance, PTCRB, GCF, operator acceptance or validated test-case claims, provide accreditation evidence, validation reports, test package option codes, test case lists, PTCRB / GCF versions and dates where applicable, because the comparison pages say those details are missing for several battle-card claims [3][37].  
- For production-path comparisons, cite formal sources for each production platform separately, because the amarisoft comparison page states that CMP180, CMP200 and CMW100 K06 production-platform specifications must each be cited from their formal source pages [3].  
- For cost, TCO, calibration-count or throughput-productivity claims, provide a formal calculation or source, because “lower TCO” and similar phrases are identified as sales language and the Anritsu page says the TCO message lacks a TCO calculation [6][66].  
- For market share or competitor market-positioning claims, provide third-party market data or official sources, because internal statements about competitor market position or market share are marked as unverified internal sales statements [23][97].

### Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a Wireless Communication competitor, use formal R&S specifications/features documents for our capabilities, competitor official documents or third-party evidence for competitor capabilities, and test-condition evidence for every numeric or superiority claim; internal battle cards alone are sales positioning, not binding technical specifications [1][4][31].
### Required evidence
- Use official R&S specifications and features documents for R&S product claims, because CMX500, CMW500, CMP180, CMP200 and related pages state that battle-card pages cannot replace formal specifications or features documents [2][6][33].  
- For CMX500 claims, cite the CMX500 Specifications Version 11.00 for binding specifications and the CMX500 Features and Functions document for signaling, application, measurement and software options [70][103].  
- Treat CMX500 Features and Functions as a features overview, because it is not a technical specifications datasheet and data without tolerance limits is not binding [70].  
- For CMX500 signaling claims, cite the listed CMX500 signaling option codes such as WLAN signaling options and LTE / NR signaling options only where those options are stated [72].  
- For CMX500 WLAN signaling and measurement claims, cite the passage that states support for 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, 802.11bn, AP testing, station testing, 2x2 MIMO, encryption/authentication, TX measurements and bandwidths up to 320 MHz [36].  
- For non-signaling or production tester claims, cite CMP180 sources only for CMP180 capabilities, because CMP180 is described as a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing with RF generator/analyzer, communication-standard measurement options, waveform options and R&S VSE analysis capability [25].  
- For CMP180 measurement-range or tolerance claims, cite the CMP180 specifications document, because the CMP180 Features and Functions document says measurement ranges and tolerance limits must be checked in specifications document PD 3609.7348.22 [57].  
- For CMP180 port and simultaneous TX/RX claims, cite the CMP180 specifications passage that states simultaneous receiver and transmitter testing and the RF generator/analyzer port structure [54].  
- For CMP200 non-signaling FR2 claims, cite the passage that states CMP200 with CMPHEAD30 / CMPHEAD50 forms a 5G NR FR2 nonsignaling one-box test solution for R&D RF parametric testing and manufacturing high-volume RF parametric testing [46].  
- For CMP200 guaranteed-performance claims, cite the CMP200 product-data limitations, because specifications with limits are guaranteed but typical, nominal and measured values are not guaranteed [47].  
- For CMW500 legacy or wireless-technology claims, cite the CMW500 support summary only where it states GSM, NB-IoT, WCDMA, LTE, NR Sub-6GHz, Bluetooth and WLAN support contexts [12].  
- For any R&S numerical specification, include the required operating conditions such as warm-up, environmental conditions, calibration interval and internal automatic adjustments where the relevant specifications passage states those conditions [70][74].  
- Do not use “Only R&S,” “safe and future-proof choice,” “only platform,” “industry-leading,” “widest frequency range,” “lower TCO,” “fewer boxes,” “first validated,” or “leadership” as technical claims unless separate formal evidence is supplied, because these are identified as sales language or needing formal evidence [2][6][33][37].  
- For competitor claims, use competitor official datasheets, release notes, option lists, support terms or third-party evidence, because the R&S battle-card claims about amarisoft, Anritsu and Keysight are stated to need official competitor or third-party verification before use in customer documents [2][6][33].  
- For Anritsu comparisons, verify frequency range, bandwidth, data rate, option code, software tools and support model with Anritsu official datasheets, release notes or support terms, because the Anritsu page says the current weakness narrative is based only on an R&S internal battle card [93].
